paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God doesn't wait for your life to get comfortable before He tells you to live it. The LORD told people in exile to "Build houses and settle down. Plant gardens and eat their produce." (Jeremiah 29:5). He also told them to "Seek the prosperity of the city to which I have sent you as exiles." (Jeremiah 29:7). So wherever you are right now, even if it's not where you hoped to be, that's a place to plant something, pray for something and love somebody.

Now, the exiles had voices telling them what they wanted to hear. The LORD said, "Do not be deceived by the prophets and diviners among you," and then added, "I have not sent them." (Jeremiah 29:8-9). Hear that, baker: a comfortable message isn't the same as a true one. The way to tell the difference is to measure everything against what God has actually said, and that's why we keep coming back to His Word.

And then comes the part that makes me want to throw a whole batch in the air. "For I know the plans I have for you, declares the LORD, plans to prosper you and not to harm you, to give you a future and a hope." (Jeremiah 29:11). He says they'll find Him "when you search for Me with all your heart," and that He will be found (Jeremiah 29:13-14). Friend, waiting is not the same as being forgotten, so live fully today, keep searching for Him with everything you've got, and trust the One who keeps His promise.
